bugs.name: Organization Forgejo webhook form refers to a repository
bugs.summary: The organization webhook form uses repository-specific introductory copy.
bugs.expected: The organization-level webhook form should refer to the organization or its repositories.
bugs.actual: The form says “Integrate Forgejo into your repository.”
reproSteps: Create a disposable organization and open Settings > Webhooks.
Read the introductory copy above Target URL.

bugs.name: Webhook help claims POST even for GET webhooks
bugs.summary: Repository Webhooks help says requests are POST even when a saved Forgejo webhook uses GET.
bugs.expected: Describe webhooks without falsely restricting the supported HTTP method to POST.
bugs.actual: The list says “Webhooks automatically make HTTP POST requests” after saving a GET webhook.
reproSteps: As a repository administrator, open Settings > Webhooks > Add webhook > Forgejo.
Use https://example.com/get-hook, choose GET and save the webhook; do not trigger delivery.
Read the Webhooks list description, which still claims POST requests.

bugs.name: Packagist validation re-enables an unchecked webhook
bugs.summary: Submitting a Packagist webhook with an invalid package URL re-checks Active, despite the user unchecking it; the error form retains the other values and remains available for correction.
bugs.expected: After rejecting the invalid package URL, the form should retain the user’s unchecked Active selection while allowing correction.
bugs.actual: The form displayed a package URL validation error and retained the entered values, but Active changed from unchecked to checked. The error and checked state persisted after waiting, and the same behavior occurred in a second fresh form.
reproSteps: Using the authenticated admin account loaded from the supplied saved authentication state, open /user/settings/hooks.
Enter a fresh dummy Packagist username and dummy API token, and set Packagist package URL to `not-a-url`.
Uncheck Active and verify it is visibly unchecked before submitting.
Click the form’s Add webhook button.
Observe the invalid-URL validation response: the other entered values remain, but Active is checked again. The error and checked state remain visible after waiting.

bugs.name: Clearing optional Microsoft Teams webhook authorization header does not persist
bugs.summary: Clearing the optional Authorization header on the newly created inactive Microsoft Teams webhook shows an update-success message, but the old header returns immediately and remains after a page refresh.
bugs.expected: After saving the edit with Authorization header empty, the field should remain empty. The form says the header is included in requests “when present,” indicating it can be omitted.
bugs.actual: The field was visibly empty before submission. The page then displayed “The webhook has been updated,” but the old value `Bearer mo-account-hook-chat2-dummy` reappeared and was still present after refreshing the edit page. The webhook remained inactive.
reproSteps: Use the authenticated admin session provided for this task (session loaded; no credentials entered).

Choose Add webhook > Microsoft Teams. Create a new inactive webhook with Target URL https://mo-account-hook-chat2-teams-7f29c4.invalid/webhook and Authorization header `Bearer mo-account-hook-chat2-dummy`; leave Active unchecked and save.
Open the edit form for this newly created fixture at /user/settings/hooks/15. Verify the Authorization header field contains the dummy value and Active is unchecked.

Clear the Authorization header field and click Update webhook. The field is visibly blank before submission; the page reports “The webhook has been updated,” then repopulates it with the previous dummy value.
Refresh the same edit page and confirm the Authorization header still contains `Bearer mo-account-hook-chat2-dummy` while Active remains unchecked.
